Even if the checksum were 'SKIP', that would not affect the safety of `--printsrcinfo`, as no download occurs during this phase. There is no evidence of malicious code execution at parse time.

Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction poses no risk.
</details>

The use of MD5 instead of SHA-256 is a weaker checksum choice but does not constitute a security threat on its own, especially since the source comes from a known and appropriate upstream (linuxmint/pix). There is no evidence of supply-chain tampering, backdoors, or data exfiltration. The package follows typical AUR packaging practices and appears to be safe.
